title: Self-healing change controller for cost-aware safety and state reconciliation
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build an autonomous change controller that applies configuration updates with cost-aware triggers, multi-signal guardrails, and deterministic state reconciliation. The controller should 1) synthesize probabilistic triggers from telemetry (cost per token, prefix cache hit rate, latency p95, model quality regressions), 2) apply changes in staged modes (dry-run, shadow-apply, limited-traffic canary), 3) automatically and safely quarantine or reconcile state when divergence is detected, and 4) surface human approvals for high-impact rollbacks. Goal: reduce manual interventions for config churn while bounding economic risk and preventing silent regressions to inference quality or latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes a composite anomaly score combining cost, latency, and quality signals and exposes it via the console dashboard.
Automated staged apply flow implemented: dry-run -> shadow-apply -> 1% traffic canary -> gradual rollout with hysteresis and economic throttle.
Automatic quarantine behavior that isolates KV/prefix cache and replays replayable requests without global rollout reversal.
Rollback and roll-forward actions are idempotent and recorded in audit logs with a unique change token for each deployment.
Runbook and emergency abort path documented; mean time to safe rollback under 5 minutes for class-high events in the staging path.
Integration tests covering cost spike, cache-corruption, model-quality regression, and cross-region failover scenarios are passing in CI.
progress_updates: 2025-11-21: Kickoff spec reviewed with product and SRE; agreed on composite anomaly scoring and economic hysteresis thresholds.
2025-11-24: Spike finished — validated cost/latency signals extraction from existing telemetry pipeline; prototyped score normalization in Python.
2025-11-26: Shadow-apply prototype built in staging cluster; observed deterministic cache diffs for KV-prefetch toggles.
2025-11-28: Safety gate logic implemented (dry-run comparisons + divergence threshold); started writing integration tests for cache quarantine behavior.
2025-11-30: First canary rollout automation wired with console canary controls; wiring for audit event formatting completed.
decisions: Use a weighted composite anomaly score instead of single-signal thresholds to reduce false positives from transient noise.
Economic hysteresis: require a sustained 3-sample window of signal breach before auto-escalation, with an override for critical security/config-only changes.
Prefer quarantining affected KV/prefix cache shards and routing around them instead of blanket global rollbacks for cache-corruption cases.
Human approval required for automatic rollback if estimated cost impact > $5000/day or customer-impact is high.
technical_notes: Composite score components: cost_per_token (linear normalized), latency_p95 (z-score), cache_hit_rate_delta (inverted), eval_quality_delta (BLEU/ROUGE-like surrogate).
State reconciliation approach: periodic snapshot checkpoints + change token model; on divergence run deterministic replayer that attempts soft-forward merges before full rollback.
Safe-apply controls implemented as an orchestrator state machine (dry-run, shadow, canary, ramp) with explicit abort and rollback transitions.
Audit events must include: change_token, actor, config_delta, pre_apply_snapshot_id, post_apply_snapshot_id, composite_score_at_apply.
Integration with console: expose 'expected economic delta' preview computed by offline simulator using recent token distribution traces.
risks: False positives leading to unnecessary rollbacks and customer-visible disruption if anomaly scoring is too sensitive.
Edge cases where replay is non-deterministic (external side-effects) could prevent automatic reconciliation and require manual intervention.
Performance overhead from continuous snapshotting and replaying if not rate-limited for high-throughput customers.
Mis-estimation of cost impact for mixed model workloads may cause thresholds to be ineffective.
mitigations: Calibrate composite score weights using 4 weeks of historical incidents and run A/B trials comparing single-signal alarms with composite alarms.
Add explicit labels/metadata for non-replayable changes; such changes bypass automatic reconciliation and require human review.
Implement adaptive snapshot cadence based on customer traffic profile and change frequency to bound overhead.
Include conservative estimation fallback and require human approval for deployments where cost estimator confidence < 0.7.
